chunks: ʿAlī, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: concerning

A man whose back is broken—he said: “For it there is the full diyah. For the two eyes, there is the diyah, and for one of them, half of the diyah. For the two ears, there is the diyah, and for one of them, half of the diyah. For the male organ, if the glans and what is above it are cut, there is the diyah. For the nose, if the soft projecting part is cut, there is the diyah. And for the two testicles, there is the diyah.”

key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: financial compensation due for bodily injury or loss
key_terms.الْأُذُنَيْنِ: the two ears, whose total loss entails full diyah
key_terms.الْحَشَفَةُ: the glans of the male organ
key_terms.الْعَيْنَيْنِ: the two eyes, whose total loss entails full diyah
key_terms.الْمَارِنُ: the soft projecting part of the nose
key_terms.ظَهْرُهُ: his back, referring here to a grave bodily injury

ai.seo_question: What diyah is due in Shia fiqh for breaking the back or injuring major organs?
ai.summary: This hadith states legal rulings concerning diyah for major bodily injuries and organs. It specifies cases in which the full diyah is due and cases in which half of the diyah is due, forming part of the jurisprudence of bodily injury compensation.
